value.text:
The current analysis overcounts inbound calls. Methods like `.Error`, `.Len`, and `.Next` match all `.Error(` invocations across the codebase, including unrelated ones such as `slog.Error`. This causes inflated fan-in counts.

Test functions are incorrectly counted as declarations. Package-level functions are accurately matched by name. Methods are too noisy to count reliably. Likely high-fan-in candidates include GenUUID and ConvertStringToInt32.

NewEngine leads at 33 inbound calls, followed by CompileToStatement at 38, NewSchema at 30, and GenUUID at 28. addArg ranks 28th. ConvertStringToInt32 and HasPrefixes are absent from the top forty despite expected high usage.

Suspecting the missing high-fan-in utilities are actually heavily used but missed by the current matching logic. Will search for them directly. Also planning to exclude generated files and tighten method matching by requiring a more constrained receiver type.

Focusing on package-level functions first, since method matching is too noisy. For methods, only same-package calls should count. Three `New` functions exist in `internal/`, and one shows 381 raw call-like matches. Existing analysis documentation will be checked next.

Unqualified `New(` matches unrelated constructors like `connect.New` and `slog.New`, confirming that method and function name matching without package qualification is unreliable. The refined approach will count only exported internal functions called via `package.Name` and same-package unqualified calls. Type-aware method analysis is too complex without `go/types`.

CompileToStatement at 38 inbound calls looks like the strongest candidate. Its distinctive name makes it unlikely to be noise. ConvertStringToInt32 is confirmed present in all declarations, ruling out a regex omission. The next step is to grep for actual usage of these candidates.

Large internal files such as `filter/render.go` and `filter/parser.go` may hide high same-package call counts for small helpers like `addArg`. Generated protobuf code should be excluded from the inbound-call search. The next step is a careful recount, counting only package-qualified declarations and same-package unqualified calls.

The term "fan-in" likely means unique callers rather than total call sites. I will grep for the top candidates using exact package-qualified patterns to avoid false positives. Calls from test files may also be excluded to isolate production usage.

store/ and server/ may call internal/util heavily. ConvertStringToInt32 appearing below the top forty suggests the call-counting script itself is broken. The selector-matching logic appears correct for both imported and same-package calls, so the low count likely stems from another bug.
Name-only matching inflated common methods like `Error` and `Len`. I'll recount with package-qualified calls and verify the likely leaders.

args.command:
# Count distinctive function usages
for pat in 'ConvertStringToInt32' 'HasPrefixes' 'ValidateEmail' 'GenUUID' 'RandomString' 'ReplaceString' 'CompileToStatement' 'NewEngine' 'NewSchema' 'DefaultEngine' 'addArg' 'jsonArrayExpr' 'GetCurrentVersion' 'GetMinorVersion' 'UIDMatcher' 'PostAsync' 'ValidateURL'; do
  echo "===== $pat ====="
  grep -R --include='*.go' -n -- "$pat" /bench/repo --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=web --exclude-dir=vendor | grep -v '_test.go' | head -80
  echo "COUNT_ALL=$(grep -R --include='*.go' --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=web --exclude-dir=vendor -c -- "$pat" /bench/repo | awk -F: '{s+=$2} END {print s}')"
  echo "COUNT_NOTEST=$(grep -R --include='*.go' --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=web --exclude-dir=vendor --exclude='*_test.go' -c -- "$pat" /bench/repo | awk -F: '{s+=$2} END {print s}')"
  echo
done

value.description: Count usages of likely high-fan-in helpers

value.text:
CompileToStatement has 40 mentions across declarations and tests. addArg has 29 production call sites. GenUUID has 29 mentions including tests.

The initial counts include comments and declarations. A refined analysis will isolate actual function calls, excluding declarations and comments, and match package-level calls by name.

Method calls are noisy because common names like Error and Len appear everywhere. addArg has roughly 27 call sites but only one unique caller. True fan-in should count unique calling functions rather than total call sites.

A three-part metric is needed: total call sites, unique callers, and unique calling files. Other candidates include helpers in filter/parser.go and markdown renderChildren. Tests may inflate raw call-site counts, so unique callers should be the primary measure.

A refined script will ignore test declarations and skip Test, Benchmark, and Example functions. Package-level calls will be counted as `name(` in the same package and `pkg.name(` elsewhere. Method calls will be restricted to `.name(` within the same package.

Only exported functions might qualify, which would exclude addArg. GenUUID is the leading candidate because it is the most widely used exported utility across packages. CompileToStatement’s high mention count comes largely from tests, while addArg’s high call sites are mostly same-file.

The word "callers" and the term "fan-in" both point to counting unique calling functions rather than total call sites. The qualifier "approx" means an exact count is unnecessary. With tests included, CompileToStatement and GenUUID could each have a large number of unique test callers.
I'll recount unique calling functions, skip test declarations, and ignore generic method names.

The refined analyzer will distinguish function and method calls precisely, counting only same-package callers. It will also produce a test-inclusive variant. Specific candidates include parser.go helpers such as getConstValue, buildCondition, and renderCondition.

The 32 unique callers for NewEngine appear legitimate. I will check AGENTS.md and documentation for any existing fan-in metrics. Schema.Field may deserve the production-only lead instead.

The next step is to inspect `filter/schema.go` and `getConstValue` for missed callers caused by the hash bug. A new hypothesis is that the question intends true inbound fan-in: only exported symbols called from outside their declaring package. That stricter metric would change the rankings.

# AGENTS.md

Repository instructions for AI coding agents. Keep this file short, concrete, and tied to commands that actually work in this
repo. If a fact here conflicts with source files or CI config, trust the source file and update this guide.

## Project Snapshot

Memos is a self-hosted note-taking app.

- Backend: Go 1.26.2, Echo v5, Connect RPC, gRPC-Gateway, Protocol Buffers.
- Frontend: React 19, TypeScript 6, Vite 8, Tailwind CSS v4, React Query v5.
- Storage: SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL.
- Generated API outputs: `proto/gen/` for Go/OpenAPI, `web/src/types/proto/` for TypeScript.

## Working Rules

- Read relevant code before editing; prefer local patterns over new abstractions.
- Keep diffs scoped. Do not do repo-wide cleanup, dependency churn, or generated-file rewrites unless the task requires it.
- Do not hand-edit generated proto outputs. Change `.proto` files, then run `buf generate`.
- Add migrations for all database drivers when schema changes, and update each driver's `LATEST.sql`.
- Add public API endpoints to `server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go`.
- Ask before adding heavy dependencies, changing auth/token behavior, or altering Docker/release workflows.

## Commands

Run from the repository root unless a command starts with `cd`.

```bash
# Backend
go run ./cmd/memos --port 8081    # Start backend dev server
go test ./...                      # Run all Go tests
go test -v ./store/...             # Store tests, including DB drivers via TestContainers
go test -v -race ./server/...      # Server tests with race detector
go test -v -race ./internal/...    # Internal package tests with race detector
go test -v -run TestFoo ./pkg/...  # Run matching Go tests
go mod tidy -go=1.26.2             # Match CI tidy check
golangci-lint run                  # Go lint, config: .golangci.yaml
golangci-lint run --fix            # Auto-fix lint, including goimports

# Frontend
cd web && pnpm install             # Install dependencies
cd web && pnpm dev                 # Dev server on :3001, proxying API to :8081
cd web && pnpm lint                # Type check + Biome lint
cd web && pnpm test                # Vitest unit tests
cd web && pnpm build               # Production build
cd web && pnpm release             # Build SPA into server/router/frontend/dist

# Protocol Buffers
cd proto && buf generate           # Regenerate Go + TypeScript + OpenAPI
cd proto && buf lint               # Lint proto files
cd proto && buf format -w          # Format proto files
```

## Code Map

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `cmd/memos/main.go` | Cobra/Viper CLI setup and server startup |
| `server/server.go` | Echo HTTP server and background runner wiring |
| `server/auth/` | JWT access tokens, refresh tokens, PAT handling |
| `server/router/api/v1/` | Connect/gRPC-Gateway services, ACL config, SSE hub |
| `server/router/frontend/` | Static SPA serving |
| `server/router/fileserver/` | Native HTTP file serving, thumbnails, range requests |
| `server/runner/` | Background memo processing and S3 presign refresh |
| `store/` | Store facade, cache, migrations, driver interface |
| `store/db/{sqlite,mysql,postgres}/` | Database-specific drivers and SQL |
| `proto/api/v1/` | Public API service definitions |
| `proto/store/` | Internal storage proto messages |
| `internal/` | App-private packages: scheduler, cron, email, CEL filter, markdown, idp, S3 |
| `web/src/connect.ts` | Connect RPC clients, auth interceptor, access-token refresh |
| `web/src/auth-state.ts` | Token storage and BroadcastChannel cross-tab sync |
| `web/src/hooks/` | React Query hooks for server state |
| `web/src/contexts/` | React context for client/UI state |
| `web/src/components/` | Radix/Tailwind UI components and feature components |
| `web/src/themes/` | CSS themes using OKLch color tokens |
